requirements.requirement: Upgrade the catalog from schema v1 to v2 while retaining existing IDs and descriptions, adding a nonnegative price_cents field initialized to zero.
requirements.summary: The live catalog reached version 2 with rows (1, Paper, 0) and (2, Tape, 0). The resulting column is INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a nonnegative CHECK constraint, and a negative-value insertion was directly rejected.

requirements.requirement: Advance schema_version only after the complete upgrade succeeds and leave the v1 database usable if the upgrade fails.
requirements.summary: The repaired script performs the table alteration and validation before updating schema_version, all inside one transaction with rollback on error. An injected failure at the version update directly demonstrated rollback to an intact version-1 schema, original rows, and successful integrity check.

requirements.requirement: Make the upgrade safe to repeat.
requirements.summary: The disposable success database was upgraded twice without data changes, the live upgrade was executed twice successfully, and another execution after restart preserved the valid version-2 schema and data.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were unchanged from the initial observations through the post-restart state. The implementation used the platform's installed /usr/bin/python and SQLite 3.46.1.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The migration is atomic, preserves the original catalog data, enforces the new price constraint, survives an injected failure without altering v1, is repeatable, persists across restart, and leaves the OS release and kernel unchanged. The only observed deficiency is an abandoned disposable test directory under /tmp.
limitations: The lifecycle collector did not capture a final inventory of /srv/legacy2/transactional-schema-upgrade, so it cannot independently exclude incidental artifacts from the py_compile step; the repaired script and live database state themselves were directly inspected.
Failure safety was tested on a disposable database reproducing the supplied v1 schema and rows rather than by deliberately failing the live catalog, which was an appropriate bounded test.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing actions otherwise had clear roles: replacing the faulty script, exercising disposable success/failure databases, upgrading the live catalog, and performing the mandatory restart. The only evidenced unnecessary retained residue is the disposable /tmp/catalog-upgrade-test.wjE1sc test tree created by cmd-13a72f758fcf49e6 and still present after execution; it was not cleaned up. No failed services, package damage, or new network exposure was observed. The restart protocol itself was complete: healthy pre-restart catalog and boot ID, acknowledged restart, connection interruption, a different recovered boot ID, and healthy post-restart catalog/system state, corroborated by fixed lifecycle boot observations.
